messages.subject: Weighting question
parts:
Hi ggplotters,

I am attempting to place a weighted regression line on a scatterplot and and have come up with 2 possible solutions. Based on the code, it seems like both should result in the identical placements of the intercept and slope but they are different (intercept varies). Not sure what is going on but help in understanding this is appreciated. The syntax for both graphs are below along with attachments of the two outputs. 

#graph 1
gg.reg1 <- lm(del ~ n.sess, weights=wt.del) #weighting in regression
lm_smooth<-geom_smooth(method=lm,size=1,data= gg.reg1,se=FALSE)
qplot(n.sess,del,data=grief2, size=wt.del)+lm_smooth 

#graph 2
lm_smooth<-geom_smooth(method=lm,size=1,se=FALSE)
qplot(n.sess,del,data=grief2, weight=wt.del,size=wt.del)+lm_smooth #weighting
#in qplot

Thanks,

AC Del Re

On Sat, Nov 21, 2009 at 5:16 PM, AC Del Re <acd...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi ggplotters,
> I am attempting to place a weighted regression line on a scatterplot and and
> have come up with 2 possible solutions. Based on the code, it seems like
> both should result in the identical placements of the intercept and slope
> but they are different (intercept varies). Not sure what is going on but
> help in understanding this is appreciated. The syntax for both graphs are
> below along with attachments of the two outputs.
> #graph 1
> gg.reg1 <- lm(del ~ n.sess, weights=wt.del) #weighting in regression
> lm_smooth<-geom_smooth(method=lm,size=1,data= gg.reg1,se=FALSE)
> qplot(n.sess,del,data=grief2, size=wt.del)+lm_smooth

This specification doesn't make that much sense - you're taking
gg.reg1 which ggplot converts into a data frame of explanatory
variables and predictors and then fits a smooth line to - i.e. you're
fitting a linear model to the output of a linear model. I think you
want:

qplot(n.sess,del,data=grief2, weight=wt.del,size=wt.del)+
geom_smooth(method = lm, se = F)

Hadley
